claims.text: IFRC/Palang Merah Indonesia situation report 'IDN: Fire - 07-2026 - Indonesia: Forest Fires and Haze in Sumatra and Kalimantan' (originally published 24 August 2026): Since mid-July 2026, forest and land fires have increased across parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan amid prolonged dry conditions; the Government of Indonesia has prioritized response operations in six provinces (Riau, Jambi, South Sumatra, West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan). As of 9 August 2026, the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) reported approximately 48,889.69 hectares burned across the six priority provinces; PMI West Kalimantan, citing the Ministry of Forestry's SIPONGI monitoring platform, separately reported approximately 38,301.86 hectares burned in West Kalimantan alone. In Central Kalimantan, the provincial disaster management agency reported 858 detected hotspots, 53 recorded fire incidents and approximately 190.96 hectares burned as of 23 August, with 66,679 acute respiratory infection cases recorded during the monitoring period (attribution to smoke exposure not yet verified). No consolidated and verified figures on people affected, displaced, injured, missing or deceased were available at the time of reporting.

Save the Children, published via ReliefWeb (7 September 2026, 'Indonesia wildfire haze threatens children across SE Asia and closes schools'): Haze from wildfires across Indonesia's Kalimantan and Sumatra regions, intensified by El Nino-driven dry conditions, has forced more than 1.4 million students in affected areas of Indonesia into online or remote learning, with about 12,800 schools across Borneo and Sumatra closed, according to government data. The haze had spread as far as the Philippines, more than 800 km (497 miles) away, and capital cities in Southeast Asia were ranked among the top 10 cities with the worst air pollution globally.

Save the Children, published via ReliefWeb (15 October 2026, ‘Children are being choked by toxic smoke’: Schools shut in Timor-Leste as haze from Indonesia wildfires continues to affect countries across Southeast Asia): haze from wildfires in Indonesia's Sumatra and Kalimantan, intensified by a powerful El Nino event, has forced Timor-Leste's Ministry of Education and Ministry of State Administration to shut schools nationwide for the remainder of the week and to ask families to keep children indoors and avoid outdoor physical activity. The report states intense forest and peatland fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan have triggered toxic smog across the region 'for weeks,' with major cities including Singapore and Kuala Lumpur experiencing 'very unhealthy' to hazardous air pollution levels as the haze drifted as far as Timor-Leste.

ASMC's alert page (asmc.asean.org/asmc-alerts/), checked 13 November 2026, shows the Southern ASEAN region haze alert further lowered to Level 0 (stand-down) on 12 November 2026, down from Level 1 on 5 November. The page attributes the decline to rain suppressing hotspot and haze activity, reporting hotspot counts falling to 13 on Sumatra (10 November) and 1 (11 November).

Indonesia's Ministry of Forestry reported on 5 November 2026 that SiPongi detected 215 high-confidence hotspots nationally as of 4 November at 21:00 WIB. The ministry cautioned that satellite hotspots are not counts of fires or burned area. Its 4 November field report recorded continuing suppression of subsurface peat fires in Talang Rimba and Pulau Geronggang, Ogan Komering Ilir, South Sumatra.

Indonesia's Ministry of Forestry (press release No. SP.718/HKLN/11/2026, 'Hotspot Terus Turun, Kemenhut Fokus Jaga Hutan dan Rakyat,' dated 17 November 2026) reported national high-confidence hotspots had fallen significantly by mid-November 2026, at one point dropping to 25. The Manggala Agni brigade confirmed all forest/land fire points in South Sumatra had been fully extinguished, leading BNPB to officially end its helicopter water-bombing operation there. In Central Kalimantan, the three-month emergency response status in Kotawaringin Barat ended, and Kotawaringin Timur moved from emergency into a recovery transition.

description: Regional haze conditions continued improving into mid-November 2026 after Indonesia's peat fires required ongoing suppression into early November. ASMC lowered the southern ASEAN alert from Level 1 to Level 0 (stand-down) on 12 November, citing rain that cut Sumatra hotspot counts to the single digits. Indonesia's Forestry Ministry reported on 17 November that Manggala Agni had fully extinguished all fire points in South Sumatra, ending BNPB's water-bombing operation there, while Central Kalimantan's Kotawaringin Barat district ended its fire emergency and Kotawaringin Timur moved into recovery; national high-confidence hotspots had fallen to as low as 25.

impact.summary: ASMC lowered the Southern ASEAN region haze alert to Level 0 (stand-down) on 12 November 2026, down from Level 1 a week earlier, attributing the decline to rain suppressing hotspot and haze activity; Sumatra hotspot counts fell to 13 (10 November) and 1 (11 November). Indonesia's Forestry Ministry reported on 17 November that Manggala Agni had fully extinguished all fire points in South Sumatra, ending BNPB's helicopter water-bombing operation there, and that Central Kalimantan's Kotawaringin Barat district had ended its emergency response status while Kotawaringin Timur moved into recovery; national high-confidence hotspots had fallen to as low as 25. Deaths and displacement remain unrecorded in this collection.

event.scale: ASMC regional haze alert Level 1; local peat fires ongoing

name: Forest Fires and Regional Haze — Indonesia

updates.text: Indonesia's Forestry Ministry reported 17 November that Manggala Agni fully extinguished all fire points in South Sumatra, ending BNPB's water-bombing operation there; Central Kalimantan's Kotawaringin Barat ended its fire emergency and Kotawaringin Timur moved into recovery. National hotspots fell to as low as 25, consistent with ASMC's 12 November stand-down.

ASMC further lowered the Southern ASEAN region haze alert to Level 0 (stand-down) on 12 November, down from Level 1 on 5 November, citing rain that cut Sumatra hotspot counts to 13 (10 November) and 1 (11 November). No Indonesian Forestry Ministry confirmation of local extinguishment at Talang Rimba or Pulau Geronggang has been found, so status remains ongoing.

ASMC lowered the southern ASEAN haze alert to Level 1, assessing transboundary risk as low while allowing for local smoke. Indonesia's Forestry Ministry reported continuing peat-fire suppression in Talang Rimba and Pulau Geronggang. Regional improvement does not establish local fire extinction.

Save the Children reported on 15 October that haze from Indonesia's wildfires, intensified by a powerful El Nino, forced Timor-Leste to shut schools nationwide for the week and kept air quality in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur at very unhealthy to hazardous levels, extending the crisis's regional reach beyond the Philippines.
